grammar.title: Measure words 件 and 張
grammar.explanation: In Chinese a number or 這/那 cannot sit directly in front of a noun; a measure word goes in between. 件 counts clothes and matters/affairs (一件衣服, 一件事), while 張 counts flat things such as tickets, cards, tables and chairs (一張票, 一張悠遊卡, 一張桌子). When the noun is obvious in a shop, you can drop it and just say 這件、那張.
grammar.contrast: 個 is the all-purpose measure word, but it is not a free substitute here: clothing takes 件 and flat objects take 張. What decides it is the shape/type of the noun, not how general you want to sound. Use 個 for people and objects with no special measure word.
grammar.common_error: Learners say 一個衣服 or 這個票, or leave the measure word out completely (兩衣服, 這票). After any number or 這/那 you must insert 件 or 張.

passage.title: 週末買衣服
passage.hanzi: 週末的下午，我和朋友去附近的店裡買衣服。那家店賣的衣服很漂亮，也很便宜。我看見一件紅的，很喜歡。老闆說：「你穿穿看，這件是小號的。」我穿了覺得有點小，老闆再找一件大號的，我穿起來很舒服。後來我買了兩件，用悠遊卡付錢，我們都很高興。
passage.gloss: On Saturday afternoon my friend and I went to a shop nearby to buy clothes. The clothes that shop sells are pretty and also cheap. I saw a red one and liked it a lot. The owner said, "Try it on — this one is a small." I put it on and felt it was a bit tight, so the owner found me a large, and it felt comfortable on me. In the end I bought two pieces and paid with my EasyCard. We were both very happy.

grammar.title: A 比 B + Adjective (comparison)
grammar.pattern: A + 比 + B + Adj (+ 一點/多了)
grammar.explanation: To say A is more ... than B, put 比 between the two things and then the adjective. The adjective goes bare — no 很, no 非常 in front of it. You can add 一點 after the adjective to say 'a bit more'. For the superlative, use 最 + Adj instead: 最便宜 = the cheapest.
grammar.contrast: 比 vs 最: 比 needs two items and says which one is more (白的比紅的便宜 = the white one is cheaper than the red one); 最 picks the top of a whole group and takes no second item (白的最便宜 = the white one is the cheapest). If you can say 'than X', use 比; if you mean 'of them all', use 最.
grammar.common_error: Learners say 我比他很高 or 我比他非常高. Degree words like 很 and 非常 cannot appear inside a 比 sentence — say 我比他高 or 我比他高一點.

grammar.title: 它 for things and animals
grammar.explanation: 它 is the third-person pronoun for objects and animals. It sounds the same as 他/她 but is written with 宀. In Taiwan it is used mostly for a thing already mentioned: 這個包包很漂亮,它是我媽買的。
grammar.contrast: 他/她 are for people; 它 is for things and animals. Same sound, different character — the choice is only visible in writing.
grammar.common_error: Learners overuse 它 as an object, saying 我很喜歡它 for every 'I like it'. In natural Mandarin the object is often just left out: 我很喜歡 or 我喜歡那個。

passage.title: 週末去逛逛
passage.hanzi: 週末我和姐姐去台北逛逛。店裡有很多衣服,我看了一件紅的,也看了一件白的。紅的非常漂亮,白的比紅的便宜一點。姐姐說白的最好看,最後我買了白的那件,它真的很舒服。回家的時候我們搭捷運,我非常高興。
passage.gloss: On the weekend my older sister and I went to look around in Taipei. The shop had lots of clothes; I looked at a red one and also a white one. The red one was extremely pretty, and the white one was a bit cheaper than the red one. My sister said the white one looked the best, so in the end I bought the white one — it really is comfortable. We took the MRT home, and I was very happy.

grammar.title: 送給 / 寄給 — marking the person who receives
grammar.pattern: S + 送/寄/買/賣 + 給 + 人 + 東西　(也可以說：S + 送 + 人 + 東西)
grammar.explanation: After a verb of handing over or sending, 給 introduces the person who gets the thing. The person comes straight after 給, then the thing. 送給 means to give as a present (no money), 寄給 means to send/mail to someone. With 送 you can also drop 給: 我送他一本書 = 我送給他一本書. Another common order puts the thing first and the 給-phrase at the end: 我買了一杯茶給她。
grammar.contrast: 給 on its own is a full verb meaning 'hand over' (請給我一張票). 送給 adds the 'as a gift' sense, and 寄給 the 'mail it' sense. If the other person pays you, the verb must be 賣, not 送.
grammar.common_error: Learners put the object before the person after 給: ✗ 我送給一本書他. The person always comes right after 給 — 我送給他一本書 — or move the whole 給-phrase to the end: 我送一本書給他。

grammar.title: 可以 — permission and possibility
grammar.pattern: S + 可以 + V；問句：…可以…嗎？／可不可以…？
grammar.explanation: 可以 before a verb asks for or gives permission, or says something is a workable option. The negative is 不可以 (not allowed).
grammar.contrast: 會 is about learned ability (我會說中文), 能 is about physical possibility or being free to do it; 可以 is mainly about permission or an acceptable option.
grammar.common_error: Saying ✗ 我可以說中文 when you mean 'I can speak Chinese' (ability). That should be 我會說中文。

passage.title: 給媽媽的生日
passage.hanzi: 這個星期天是我媽媽的生日。早上我騎腳踏車去附近的店，買了一件很漂亮的衣服送給她，九十元，真的很便宜。我還買了一杯珍珠奶茶給她喝。晚上我們一家人可以一起去餐廳吃飯。媽媽很高興，她說這是她最好的生日。
passage.gloss: This Sunday is my mom's birthday. In the morning I rode my bike to a shop nearby and bought a very pretty piece of clothing to give her — ninety dollars, really cheap. I also bought her a cup of bubble tea to drink. In the evening our whole family can go out to a restaurant together. My mom was very happy; she said it was her best birthday.
